title: Zero Array Transformation III
statement:
`nums` is an array of integers, and each entry `queries[i] = [l_i, r_i]` of `queries` is an inclusive range of its indices. Using a query means lowering every element whose index lies in its range by either `0` or `1`, chosen separately for each of those indices; each query you keep is used exactly once.

You may discard some of the queries. Return the largest number of queries you can discard so that the queries you keep can still make every element of `nums` equal to `0`. If even keeping all of the queries cannot do this, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

Discarding as many queries as possible means keeping as few as possible while each index `i` stays covered by at least `nums[i]` kept queries (extra coverage is harmless, since a query may skip an index). Trying every subset is exponential.

Sweep the indices left to right. When index `i` is covered fewer than `nums[i]` times, another query that starts at or before `i` must be kept. Of those, the one reaching farthest right is never a worse pick: it covers `i` whenever any of them does, plus every later index the others cover. A max-heap of right ends finds it quickly.

## Approach

1. Sort `queries` by left end, so they can be offered to the sweep in order.
2. At index `i`, push the right end of every query starting at or before `i` onto the max-heap `heap`.
3. `cover` counts the kept queries covering `i`; the difference array `diff` drops each kept query once its range is over.
4. While `cover < nums[i]`: if the heap is empty or its largest right end is before `i`, nothing can help, so return `-1`. Otherwise pop that `end` and keep the query (`cover++`, `diff[end + 1]--`, `used++`).
5. Return `queries.length - used`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 0, 2]`, sorted queries `[[0, 2], [0, 2], [1, 1]]`. At `i = 0` both `[0, 2]` queries enter the heap; `cover = 0 < 2`, so both are kept (`used = 2`, `diff[3] = -2`). At `i = 1` the end `1` is pushed, but `nums[1] = 0` needs nothing. At `i = 2`, `cover = 2` meets `nums[2] = 2`. The answer is `3 - 2 = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + q log q): sorting, plus at most one push and one pop per query.
- Space: O(n + q) for `diff` and the heap.

## Pitfalls

- Pick by farthest right end, not by input order or by shortest range.
- Queries whose range ended before `i` may stay in the heap; as the top is the largest end, `heap[0] < i` means none can help.
- A kept query must stop counting after its range: `diff[end + 1]--`.
- Return the number discarded, `queries.length - used`, not the number kept.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `heap` | max-heap of right ends of queries that have started but are not kept |
| `push`, `pop` | add a right end; remove and return the largest one |
| `diff` | difference array that drops kept queries after their range ends |
| `next` | index of the next sorted query to offer to the sweep |
| `cover` | number of kept queries covering index `i` |
| `used` | number of queries kept so far; `end` is the right end of the latest one |
